links.targetTitle: The voter-facing Executive Document is reviewed only inside

title: No actor may both author and approve the same content within one Executive cycle
content:
The same structural rule appears at three unrelated points in the chunk, which is what makes it a pattern rather than a provision:

- **A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2** — "The Spell Team not involved in the technical Forum Post creation must confirm the contents of the Forum Post as a public reply."
- **A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.2.1** — a Prime Agent's draft Forum posts must be internally reviewed "by at least one member of the Prime Agent's team independent of the action's author."
- **A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.3** — a Prime Spell reviewer must be "a member of a Core Spell Team that is **not** also serving as the Crafter for the Sky Core Spell of the same Executive Vote cycle, or an external reviewer engaged for the purpose."

The third instance is the most instructive because the disqualification is scoped to the cycle, not to the role. A Core Spell Team member is a perfectly acceptable reviewer — unless they are crafting the Spell this same cycle. Independence is treated as a property of a specific pairing at a specific time rather than a permanent job description.

That scoping is what makes the rule survivable in a small ecosystem. A permanent separation of authorship and review would require two disjoint pools of scarce specialists; a per-cycle rotation gets the same independence guarantee from one pool. The cost is that compliance is invisible from the artifact alone — it must be checked against who did what this week.
description: Recurs three times: forum posts confirmed by uninvolved Spell Team members, drafts reviewed by a non-author, and Prime Spell reviewers barred from crafting that cycle's Sky Core Spell.
